synthesis.intent_alignment: Searchers typing 'house cleaning aspendale' are almost entirely local-service seekers wanting a bookable cleaner in their suburb (the SERP is dominated by local_pack + suburb-specific service pages), but the DataForSEO intent classifiers disagree on label — google_keyword_overview tags it 'navigational' (foreign_intent: commercial) while dataforseo_labs_search_intent tags it 'informational' (0.48) with a close secondary 'commercial' (0.442) — so treat this as a low-volume, commercial-navigational local search rather than research-stage informational, and note the classifier disagreement explicitly rather than picking one label with false confidence.
competitor_takeaways: ELM Cleaning differentiates with a specific guarantee (24-hour re-clean) and a broader service bundle (regular + NDIS + end-of-lease) on one Aspendale page — a single strong guarantee stated locally out-performs generic trust copy

Jim's Cleaning and Airtasker win on sheer social proof (3,096 and 16-69 reviews respectively across variants) — the client cannot compete on volume yet, so the page should lean on rating (5-star) and specificity (dedicated pairs team, membership) instead of count

Move Clean and Jim's Cleaning both run separate, keyword-matched End-of-Lease Aspendale pages rather than folding bond-clean into the general house-cleaning page — worth considering as its own internal link/section given how much SERP real estate end-of-lease occupies

ServiceSeeking and ServiceSeeking-style aggregators win on price transparency (explicit $/hr and $/service bands) — the client's fixed, all-inclusive membership pricing is a genuine differentiator if stated plainly rather than hidden behind a quote request
